newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Jan-Feb tourism drops 17.4 pct - statistics.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Jan-Feb tourism drops 17.4 pct - statistics.

text.p: Yugoslavia registered a total of 302,635 tourists in the first two months of 1997, a drop of 17.4 percent against the same period last year, the Federal Statistics Office reported on Thursday.
Of the total, Yugoslavs numbered 265,930, or 19 percent less than in the January-February period 1996.
The number of visitors from other former Yugoslav republics -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- rose 9.8 percent to 19,658 against the same period last year.
The number of foreign tourists dropped 17 percent against last year's figure to 17,047, continuing the downward trend registered in January.
Most foreign visitors, or 2,324, came from Italy, followed by Bulgaria with 1,466, Greece with 1,332, Germany with 1,289 and Austria with 1,259.
According to the National Bank of Yugoslavia figures, hard currency income from tourism in January 1997 was $2.1 million, which is 32.3 percent less than in January 1996.
NOTE -- Data is based on reception figures from hotels and other accommodation facilities. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4254
